topic: What if you never needed to sleep?
title: WHAT IF YOU NEVER
NEEDED TO SLEEP?

power.sound: a wall switch click, then the room drops into silence
power.look: the building's windows die in a sweep, one amber window stays on, and Pip's eyes catch amber
power.rule: Everyone else still shuts down. You never do.

script.text: Lights out. You beat the game.
Lights out. You stand there, watching them breathe.
What if you never needed to sleep?
But sleep is at least four hundred fifty million years old. Even jellyfish do it. No brain. That's real.
You should be the only one who doesn't.
So who's that, waving at you?

science.claim: Sleep is at least 450 million years old.
science.working: Leung et al. recorded sleep-state brain activity in zebrafish that resembles slow-wave and REM sleep in land vertebrates. Fish and land vertebrates last shared an ancestor at least 450 million years ago, so the researchers date these neural sleep patterns to at least then. Caveat: an inference from young fish, and it dates the brain patterns, so the script keeps 'at least' and never says every animal sleeps (Stanford's own release says scientists can't say that for certain).
science.source: Leung et al., Nature 2019; Stanford Medicine release, 'Neural sleep patterns emerged at least 450 million years ago', via ScienceDaily 10 Jul 2019

science.claim: Even jellyfish do it, and they have no brain.
science.working: Cassiopea, the upside-down jellyfish, has a diffuse nerve net and no central brain. It met three behavioural tests for a sleep-like state: reduced activity at night, slower response to a stimulus, and rebound after being deprived of rest. The paper's term is 'sleep-like state'.
science.source: Nath et al., 'The Jellyfish Cassiopea Exhibits a Sleep-like State', Current Biology, 21 Sep 2017

science.working: The premise, not a measurement: the hours a person who sleeps eight hours gets back. No statistic is claimed.

shots.note: The block at night, every window lit. On 'out' they die in a sweep. One amber window stays on.
Pip on the sofa in the dark, pad in hand, TV light on his face, eyes amber.
The TV fills the frame: the boss's bar empties, it bursts, YOU WIN. Thumbs mash in the blurred foreground.
Mum's hand flips the hall switch. Warm wall goes dark.
Pip fumbles a chord, tongue-out effort, a string pings loose.
Pip rocks out, foot on the amp, guitar up, the moon behind him.
Sis asleep with the cat on the duvet. Her nightlight clicks off.
The door creaks open. A tall dark figure in the hall light, two amber eyes.
Pip's face half in the dark, unblinking, a slow head tilt. Uneasy.
The dark block, one window lit, the title over the sky.
Time-lapse: the sun comes up fast behind Pip, +8H pops up three times, arms up.
A line of sleeping animals running back 450,000,000 years, ending at a wide-awake YOU.
A jellyfish pulsing slowly. A scan ring finds no brain: BRAIN 0.
Pip at his window, the block opposite all dark. In the pause one window clicks on, cold white.
Pip's face in the cold light, shock.

shots.size: extreme zoom on the far window
shots.note: A figure in a suit, dark against the light, waves. Amber eyes. Click: the window dies, the eyes stay a beat, then black.
